look_here_first: FIRST inspect a mid-stem leaf's two surfaces and edge: S. lanceolatum generally has pliable, nonwaxy, comparatively flat leaves with diffuse or elongated lower-surface vein AREOLES, unlike S. praealtum with firmer waxy upper faces and conspicuous small isodiametric lower areoles. For subsp. lanceolatum verify outer phyllaries ~1/3–2/3 inner (not the mostly 2/3+ of subsp. hesperium) and no big leafy bract directly subtending the head. Do NOT use peduncle bract counts for a hard split; the FNA genus key conflicts with its species treatments.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: tall rhizomatous perennial; moist-ground habitat; narrow lanceolate leaves; many small white-rayed heads; broad paniculate inflorescence

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: Use growth form, leaf shape, panicle architecture, and infraspecific characters together; species-level white aster appearance is not enough for subspecies assignment.

lookalikes.differences: S. praealtum shows firm, waxy often rolled-margin leaves and clear small regular vein areoles below; S. lanceolatum generally pliable nonwaxy flat leaves and faint/elongate areoles. FNA GENUS key says praealtum 1–3 vs lanceolatum 5–12+ bracts, but FNA SPECIES descriptions say reverse; don't teach bract count as exclusive. Nominate subspecies needs outer/inner phyllary ratio confirmation and provenance (hesperium has long outer phyllaries and leafy head bracts).
